title: improv·artist · geometric (Lygia Clark)
mutation_directive: improv artist: geometric via Lygia Clark

improv_extras.practice: neo-concrete folded metal; bichos that the viewer reshapes

v1.feedback: The hinged-plane concept maps well to Clark's bichos, but the flat initial state reads as a bland grid of gray rectangles — the form needs a default partially-folded pose so the articulation is visible within 2 seconds without user interaction. The palette is appropriately restrained but too monochrome; Clark's later bichos used contrasting metal finishes and occasional color planes — introduce one warm accent (oxidized copper, matte red) on a single panel to create focal hierarchy. Edge-density bias is a nice touch, but the z-thickness is nearly zero so the planes look paper-thin even when folded; give each panel a slight extrusion (0.3–0.5 units) so folds cast visible particle-depth shadows. Finally, the autonomous animation is just a gentle Z-rotation — add a slow, looping fold cycle (sinusoidal uFold1/uFold2 modulation) so the piece breathes dimensionally when idle, proving the hinge mechanic without requiring drag interaction.

v2.feedback: The hinged-panel hierarchy and click-to-refold interaction genuinely channel Clark's participatory Bichos — good structural fidelity. However, all 12 panels are identical rectangles, which reads more like an unfolding cardboard box than Clark's irregular, biomorphic metal cuts; vary panel aspect ratios and add occasional triangular or trapezoidal faces to break the grid. The silver/copper palette is restrained and material-appropriate, but the depth shading alone doesn't sell the metallic surface — add a simple Fresnel-like rim brightening in the fragment shader so edges catch light and the folded planes read as reflective sheet metal rather than matte card. Consider tightening the camera or scaling the structure so the sculpture fills more vertical frame area during deep folds.
